name: Thyme
description: Thyme (Thymus vulgaris) is a popular, fragrant herb commonly used in cooking. It is widely recognized as non-toxic and safe for cats. Its leaves, stems, and flowers do not contain any compounds known to be poisonous to felines. If a cat decides to nibble on a thyme plant, there is no cause for alarm regarding toxicity. For most cats, a small taste of the leaves will not cause any issues. As with any plant material, eating a very large quantity might lead to mild, temporary stomach upset, such as vomiting or diarrhea, but this is a general reaction to overeating plant matter, not a sign of poisoning. Home gardeners can feel confident growing thyme in spaces shared with cats. It is a safe, pet-friendly choice for an indoor or outdoor herb garden.
